method: Node-driven manual renders (same method as reports/perf-after.json). Camera re-set inside EVERY timed iteration (the live rAF loop moves it otherwise — see cross-check). SwiftShader = LOWER BOUND, not game performance.

avenue_calls.note: +8 = 5 new traffic cars + peds now spread across districts; triangles 538040 -> 540736 (+0.5%).

city_calls.note: NOT like-for-like: the baseline 238 came from a staged markings-audit top shot (camera unknown, likely frustum-limited); this run's city camera (0,200,40)->(0,0,0) sees the WHOLE 240x140m map at once. The 983 is the honest whole-city number under this camera — OVER the 600 budget, OPEN.

promenade_calls.note: No baseline for this camera. 655 is OVER the 600 budget — OPEN (street-level promenade sees casino + hotel + marina + quay at once).

ring_calls.note: No baseline for this camera. Under 600.

ms_frame.note: NOT comparable to baseline: perf-after.json timed renders from Node (CDP round-trip + main-thread contention under the live rAF loop, 4-8 s per render). This run times the render call in-page (median 6-26 ms). The render call itself is fast; the cost is the SwiftShader software rasterizer + loop contention, not the game.

verdict: Avenue 400 and ring 201 under 600. Promenade 655 and whole-city 983 OVER 600 under these cameras — OPEN: needs mesh merging / instancing / LOD or a re-check of what camera the 600 budget was measured with. The +5 traffic cars cost ~8 draw calls at avenue scale.
